description: Drop-in replacement for Requests. Automatic HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3. WebSocket, and SSE included. WASI Supported.

summary.one_liner: Niquests is a drop-in replacement for the Requests HTTP library in Python, adding HTTP/2, HTTP/3, async sessions, WebSocket and SSE support.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a Requests-style API (get, post, sessions, params, data, json) for Python, with an async counterpart via AsyncSession. The README says it negotiates HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 automatically and includes WebSocket and SSE support. It lists DNS over HTTPS, QUIC, TLS and UDP, OCSP and CRL revocation checks, DNSSEC, ECH, and post-quantum security options. Other listed features include SOCKS proxy support, Happy Eyeballs, streaming downloads, multipart uploads, cookie persistence, and .netrc handling. The README says existing test mocking tools such as betamax, requests-mock and responses still work with it.
use_cases: replace requests in an existing Python project
make async HTTP calls with asyncio
call HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 APIs from Python
consume WebSocket or server-sent events streams
query DNS over HTTPS or QUIC
run HTTP client code in WASI or Pyodide environments
notable: Drop-in replacement for Requests, with import niquests as requests suggested for migration
Automatic HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 support, with HTTP/2 by default
Async API via AsyncSession alongside the sync interface
Multiple DNS transports (DoH, DoQ, DoT, UDP) plus DNSSEC
Works with betamax, requests-mock and responses according to the README
caveats: HTTP/3 support is installed only if the platform can support it natively, such as with a pre-built wheel
Official Python support is stated as 3.7+ for Python or PyPy
Presented as a fork of Requests, which is itself in feature freeze
